analysis: The problem is complete and the full answer is objectively checkable. The polynomial \(P(x) = x^n - 5x + 4\) can be factored as \(P(x) = (x-1)(x^{n-1} + x^{n-2} + \cdots + x - 4)\). For \(P(x)\) to have all integer roots, the polynomial \(x^{n-1} + x^{n-2} + \cdots + x - 4\) must also have integer roots. The only integer root of \(x^{n-1} + x^{n-2} + \cdots + x - 4\) is \(x = 1\), because substituting \(x = 1\) gives \(1^{n-1} + 1^{n-2} + \cdots + 1 - 4 = n - 4\), which must be zero for \(x = 1\) to be a root. Therefore, \(n = 4\). For \(n = 4\), the polynomial becomes \(P(x) = (x-1)(x^3 + x^2 + x - 4)\), and the roots are \(x = 1\) and the roots of \(x^3 + x^2 + x - 4\). The polynomial \(x^3 + x^2 + x - 4\) can be factored as \((x-1)(x^2 + 2x + 4)\), and the roots of \(x^2 + 2x + 4\) are not integers. Therefore, the only positive integer value of \(n\) for which \(P(x)\) has all integer roots is \(n = 4\).
